# Record missing native dependency sources instead of treating wrappers as complete ports

## Platform difference

A repository with OH Dart/native wrapper code may still depend on unavailable local packages, uninitialized submodules or externally built libraries.

## Implementation

Etohos references a local EasyTier HAR outside the checkout. LocalSend's Rust HTTP core is a submodule and another gitlink lacks a declared source URL. PixEz retains a developer-local FRB dependency in its inspected snapshot. Kelivo has missing ignored path dependencies and build-profile prerequisites. Venera has an unavailable local ZIP package checkout. These gaps bound what can be concluded from the visible adapters.

## Applicability

Distinguish generated SDK artifacts from missing project-owned source. An SDK-generated flutter.har can be a normal build product; an unexplained private path needs a reproducible replacement or explicit limitation.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

Do not fabricate an implementation or a clean-build guarantee from a wrapper call. Source availability alone is not a reuse license; Kelivo's unresolved license stays unresolved. Avoid executing opaque binaries to fill research gaps.

## Verification

Inventory every path dependency/gitlink/HAR, identify its source/version/license, materialize it only within the authorized build scope, and validate a clean checkout independently from an existing developer machine.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
